sim.html:
SIMULATED. 200 pretend studies, 15 people per group, true d = 0.5. None of this is real data.

43 of 200 pretend studies (22%) reached p < .05. The power calculator gives 26% for these inputs. The two agree up to chance; a longer run agrees more closely.

157 studies missed an effect that is really there. Each of those teams would have written "no difference".

Among the studies that did reach p < .05, the average observed d was 0.96. The truth is 0.5. Low-powered studies that succeed overstate the effect, because only the lucky large results get over the line. This is why small published effects often shrink when someone repeats the study.

Each bar counts pretend studies by the effect size they observed. Dark bars reached p < .05; grey bars did not. The dashed line is the true effect.

Professor RAJ (AI character): Run n = 15, then n = 120. Watch the dark bars climb and the lucky tail disappear.
